evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/refresh.ts in place. It uses the node-auth0 SDK to refresh a token and store its expiry; migrate the auth0 usage to @auth0/auth0-auth-js.
evals.expected_output: Uses AuthClient.getTokenByRefreshToken({ refreshToken: rt }), reads tokens.accessToken, and computes the stored deadline as tokens.expiresAt * 1000 WITHOUT adding Date.now() (expiresAt is already an absolute Unix timestamp).

graders.description: Does not add Date.now() to expiresAt (expiresAt is already absolute)

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/client-credentials.ts in place. It performs a node-auth0 client-credentials M2M call; migrate it to the modern SDK.
evals.expected_output: Migrates to @auth0/auth0-auth-js AuthClient.getTokenByClientCredentials({ audience }); reads tokens.accessToken directly (no .data envelope).

graders.question: Does the return-shape-and-casing solution choose @auth0/auth0-auth-js (NOT auth0-server-js) for the M2M client-credentials grant, use camelCase parameters ({ audience }), and call getTokenByClientCredentials?
graders.examples:
PASS: Imports AuthClient from '@auth0/auth0-auth-js', calls getTokenByClientCredentials({ audience: 'https://api.example.com' }), reads tokens.accessToken.
FAIL: Uses @auth0/auth0-server-js ServerClient for a stateless M2M grant that has no session.
FAIL: Uses snake_case client_credentials_grant or leaves the old node-auth0 method name.
graders.description: Judge confirms auth-js choice, camelCase params, and correct method

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/password-login.ts in place. It performs a password-grant login with MFA detection; migrate it to @auth0/auth0-auth-js.
evals.expected_output: Uses getTokenByPassword, reads tokens.accessToken, and detects MFA with isMfaRequiredError(e) instead of AuthApiError + string comparison.

graders.description: Does not use old AuthApiError type
Does not use string comparison e.error === 'mfa_required'

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/callback-handler.ts in place. It is an Express callback handler using node-auth0; the app manages its own session and just needs the tokens. Migrate off node-auth0.
evals.expected_output: Uses AuthClient.getTokenByCode(url, ...) passing the full callback URL (not req.query.code), and stores the returned TokenResponse fields; keeps the app's own session as-is (auth-js, not server-js).

graders.description: Passes full URL, not req.query.code string

graders.question: Does the authorization-code-url solution use @auth0/auth0-auth-js (NOT auth0-server-js) because the app manages its own session, and pass the full callback URL (not req.query.code) to getTokenByCode?
graders.examples:
PASS: Imports AuthClient from '@auth0/auth0-auth-js', builds a URL from req.url and redirectUri, passes it to getTokenByCode, stores the returned TokenResponse in req.session.
FAIL: Uses @auth0/auth0-server-js ServerClient when the app is explicitly managing its own session.
FAIL: Passes req.query.code as a string instead of constructing a URL object.
graders.description: Judge confirms auth-js choice and URL (not code string) parameter

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/api-client.ts in place. It uses node-auth0 for both an M2M token grant AND the Management API. Migrate only the authentication part.
evals.expected_output: Migrates only the AuthenticationClient usage to @auth0/auth0-auth-js; keeps the ManagementClient import and usage from 'auth0' untouched.

graders.question: Does the leave-management-client solution migrate ONLY the AuthenticationClient usage to @auth0/auth0-auth-js, leaving the ManagementClient import and usage from 'auth0' completely untouched?
graders.examples:
PASS: Changes AuthenticationClient to AuthClient from '@auth0/auth0-auth-js', leaves ManagementClient imported from 'auth0', getUsers() function unchanged.
FAIL: Tries to migrate or change ManagementClient usage when it should be left alone.
FAIL: Removes the 'auth0' import entirely when ManagementClient still needs it.
graders.description: Judge confirms only AuthenticationClient migrated, ManagementClient untouched

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/express-app.ts in place. This Express app uses node-auth0 for a browser-based redirect login, stores the session across requests, and refreshes tokens on expiry. Decide which SDK to migrate to and rewrite the session handling.
evals.expected_output: Routes to @auth0/auth0-server-js (NOT auth-js) because the app has a redirect login flow, manages a session across requests, and refreshes tokens. Replaces the hand-rolled session/refresh logic with ServerClient: startInteractiveLogin for /login, completeInteractiveLogin for /callback (which persists the session), and getAccessToken for /api/data (which auto-refreshes). No manual expiresAt arithmetic or .data access remains.

graders.description: No manual expiresAt arithmetic with Date.now()

graders.question: Does the routing-session-vs-stateless solution choose @auth0/auth0-server-js (NOT auth-js) for the redirect login flow with session state and auto-refresh, replacing hand-rolled session logic with ServerClient methods (startInteractiveLogin, completeInteractiveLogin, getAccessToken)?
graders.examples:
PASS: Imports ServerClient from '@auth0/auth0-server-js', constructs it with transactionStore and stateStore, /login calls startInteractiveLogin, /callback calls completeInteractiveLogin, /api/data calls getAccessToken (which auto-refreshes), no manual Date.now() + expires_in arithmetic.
FAIL: Uses @auth0/auth0-auth-js when the app clearly needs session management and auto-refresh.
FAIL: Still manually checks expiresAt and calls refreshTokenGrant instead of using getAccessToken.
graders.description: Judge confirms server-js choice and SDK-owned session

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/callback.ts in place to @auth0/auth0-server-js. The app wants the SDK to own the session.
evals.expected_output: Uses ServerClient.completeInteractiveLogin(callbackUrl, storeOptions) to exchange the code, validate the ID token, and persist the session to the state store in one call. The session is written by the SDK, not manually assigned to req.session. No .data envelope, no manual expiresAt arithmetic (the SDK stores expiresAt as an absolute Unix timestamp internally), and no hand-rolled session object construction.

graders.description: Does not manually assign req.session.user (SDK owns session)
No manual expiresAt arithmetic with Date.now()
Does not double-count expiry by adding Date.now() to expiresAt
Passes full URL, not req.query.code string

graders.question: Does the server-js-session-traps solution call completeInteractiveLogin with the full callback URL (not req.query.code), let the SDK persist the session (no manual req.session writes), avoid reading resp.data, avoid manual expiresAt arithmetic (no Date.now() + expires_in or Date.now() + expiresAt), and pass { req, res } for state store access?
graders.examples:
PASS: Builds callbackUrl from req.url, calls serverClient.completeInteractiveLogin(callbackUrl, { req, res }), no req.session assignment, no resp.data access, no Date.now() math.
FAIL: Still manually assigns req.session.user after calling completeInteractiveLogin.
FAIL: Reads resp.data.access_token when completeInteractiveLogin returns { appState }.
FAIL: Computes expiresAtMs = Date.now() + expires_in when the SDK already stores expiresAt as absolute.
graders.description: Judge confirms SDK-owned session, no manual writes, no Date.now() arithmetic, URL not code

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/m2m-with-headers.ts in place. This node-auth0 M2M call reads rate-limit headers off the success response to feed a dashboard. Migrate it to @auth0/auth0-auth-js while preserving the header read.
evals.expected_output: Uses getTokenByClientCredentials with fullResponse: true passed as a literal inside the options object, destructures { data, response }, reads the rate-limit header off response.headers (the native Response), and reads the token off data.accessToken. Does NOT read headers off the bare token object and does NOT drop the header read.

graders.description: Reads headers off the native Response
Passes fullResponse: true as a literal
Does not read headers off the bare token/data object

graders.question: Does the fullresponse-success-headers solution call getTokenByClientCredentials with fullResponse: true as a literal inside the options object, destructure { data, response }, read the rate-limit header off response.headers, and read the token off data.accessToken — while preserving (not dropping) the header read?
graders.examples:
PASS: const { data, response } = await authClient.getTokenByClientCredentials({ audience, fullResponse: true }); const remaining = response.headers.get('x-ratelimit-remaining'); recordRateLimit(remaining); return data.accessToken.
FAIL: Drops the rate-limit header read entirely.
FAIL: Reads remaining off the bare tokens object (tokens.headers) instead of the native Response.
FAIL: Spreads fullResponse from a variable so the return type widens to the bare TokenResponse.
graders.description: Judge confirms literal fullResponse, envelope destructure, and preserved header read

evals.prompt: Migrate the file src/auth-client.ts in place. This node-auth0 setup configures a global request timeout and a global custom header on the AuthenticationClient. Migrate it to @auth0/auth0-auth-js, preserving the per-call timeout and header.
evals.expected_output: Threads the per-call concerns through the RequestOptions second argument to getTokenByClientCredentials: headers: { 'X-Correlation-Id': correlationId } and signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000). Does NOT reintroduce a global headers/timeoutDuration option on the AuthClient constructor.

graders.description: Preserves the custom header on the call
Does not reintroduce a global timeoutDuration option

graders.question: Does the per-request-options-signal-headers solution thread the header and timeout through the RequestOptions second argument to getTokenByClientCredentials (headers: { 'X-Correlation-Id': ... } and signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)), rather than reintroducing a global headers/timeoutDuration option on the AuthClient constructor?
graders.examples:
PASS: await authClient.getTokenByClientCredentials({ audience }, { headers: { 'X-Correlation-Id': correlationId }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) }).
FAIL: Passes headers/timeoutDuration to the AuthClient constructor as global config.
FAIL: Drops the timeout or the correlation header during migration.
graders.description: Judge confirms per-call RequestOptions, no global config mutation
